extracted.intended_audience: agency rulewriters, regulated parties, administrative-law practitioners, and public commenters interested in direct final rules and notice-and-comment procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidance and standards for agencies' use of direct final rules (DFRs): when to issue them, how to pair with companion proposed rules, how to treat comments (including significant/adverse comments), withdrawals/rescissions, and effects on effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: DFR effectiveness when no significant adverse comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If no significant adverse comments are received, the direct final rule will become effective on the date it establishes (e.g., 'if no significant adverse comments were received, the direct final rule would become effective on February 23, 2026').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies routinely state a target effective date in the DFR and confirm that the rule will take effect as scheduled absent significant adverse comments. Examples in the results show multiple agencies confirming effectiveness when no significant adverse comments were received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use DFR when action is noncontroversial / no opposing comments expected
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may issue a direct final rule when they 'believe this action is not controversial and do not expect comments that oppose it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DFRs are appropriate for actions the agency expects to be noncontroversial; the preamble may explicitly state the agency did not publish a prior proposal because it expects no opposing comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish a companion proposed rule alongside the DFR
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies often publish a companion proposed rule on the same day as the direct final rule to invite comment and provide a fallback if the DFR must be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The companion proposed rule 'invited comment on the substance of the direct final rule (as well as on additional subjects)' and serves as the procedural vehicle to resolve comments if the DFR is withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw or rescind DFR upon significant adverse comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If any significant adverse comments are received on any part of the direct final rule, the agency will publish a document rescinding that part (or parts) of the DFR and will address the comments in a subsequent final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language examples: 'if any significant adverse comments are received on any part of the Direct Final Rule, the Commission will publish a document that rescinds any such part of this action and will address the comments received in a subsequent final rule as a response to the companion proposed rule.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective withdrawal: withdraw only portions subject to significant adverse comment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a DFR addresses multiple rule changes, the agency may withdraw only the portions of the DFR that received significant adverse comments while allowing unaffected portions to proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: 'If significant adverse comments are filed only with respect to a subset of the rule revisions addressed by this Direct Final Rule, the Bureau will withdraw the portions of the Direct Final Rule that were subject to significant adverse comments.' Agencies will then publish withdrawals for those specific parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse comment triggers use of companion proposed rule for subsequent action
rubrics_metrics.description: When the DFR is withdrawn because of adverse comment, the agency will proceed with the companion proposed rule and will address the comments in a subsequent final action based on that proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples state the agency 'will address those comments in a subsequent final action, which will be based on the companion proposed rule.' The companion proposed rule thus forms the basis for further rulemaking if the DFR cannot stand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of effective date while responding to comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may delay the effective date of a direct final rule and publish a response to comments when comments are received that require consideration (e.g., 'As a result, DOE delays the effective date of the direct final rule, and is responding to the comment it received on the direct final rule').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays can be temporary (postponing the originally scheduled effective date) while the agency responds and determines whether withdrawal or revision is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No second comment period after DFR withdrawal (agency may not reopen comment period)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may state that it 'will not institute a second comment period on this subject' following withdrawal of a DFR; instead, comments submitted to the companion proposed rule will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits re‑notice: the agency uses the companion proposed rule's comment record rather than reopening a new separate comment period for the same subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic repeal or automatic effectiveness absent significant adverse comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may find prior notice and comment 'unnecessary' under the APA for certain repeals but still provide a DFR opportunity for input, with the identified rules 'automatically being repealed absent any significant adverse comments in response to this Direct Final Rule.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pattern is used when agencies conclude APA notice isn't required but nonetheless offer a DFR-based public input window; if no significant adverse comments are filed, the repeal occurs automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docketing and treatment of comments (including non‑significant comments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted are docketed (for example, 'the NRC received and docketed one comment on the companion proposed rule') and may be addressed differently depending on whether they are 'significant adverse' comments triggering withdrawal or routine comments addressed in the rulemaking record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all docketed comments will be characterized as significant adverse; agencies track which comments trigger withdrawal versus those that will be handled in the administrative record or in subsequent final actions.
